paragraphs.source_en: But early in 1963 a cleric little known outside ulema circles, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, began to preach in Qom against the shah’s government. He attacked its corruption, its neglect of the poor, and its failure to uphold Iran’s sovereignty in its relationship with the United States—and he also disliked the shah’s sale of oil to Israel. Khomeini made this move at a time when, following the death of Ayatollah Borujerdi in 1961, many Iranian Shi‘a were unclear whom to follow as marja-e taqlid. In March, on the anniversary of the martyrdom of the Emam Jafar Sadeq, troops and SAVAK agents attacked the madreseh where Khomeini was preaching and arrested him, killing several students at the same time. He was released shortly afterward but continued his attacks on the government.
